thread:
Anna C (partnerships): quick heads-up — we're planning a breaking change to the Partner API that will go out as v3. Affects auth header format + streaming payload envelopes. Need partner SDK compatibility plan and outreach. ETA: 2026-05-10 for canary rollout.
Mike L (platform): can you paste the diff or short summary? which endpoints exactly?
Anna C (partnerships): short summary: auth header moves from `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to `Authorization: Redwood-Sig <token>` (signature prefix), and streaming events now use `type: chunk` / `type: done` instead of the current newline-delimited `data:` chunks. Endpoints: /generate, /chat-stream. Full spec link: https://internal.redwood.company/partner-api/v3-spec (will post after this thread).
Sara K (integrations): timeline ok. question: can we provide a compatibility header so old SDKs keep working while partners migrate? e.g., `X-Compat: v2` fallback.
Raj P (vendor-eng): hardware partners will mostly be unaffected, but SI integrations that rely on SDKs will break if we cut without shims. We should publish SDK patches the same day as canary.
Eve M (product): propose: 6-week window — 2w notice, 4w dual-support overlap, then enforce. Partners get deprecated warnings in-console during overlap. Thoughts?
Mike L (platform): we can add a runtime compatibility shim in the API gateway to accept old `Authorization: Bearer` for the overlap, but that buys risk/complexity. Alternative: auto-detect client stream format and translate server-side for 4w. Which do we prefer?
Anna C (partnerships): prefer translation layer for streaming only, keep auth switch explicit (encourage partners to upgrade). translation + SDK shims seems safest.
Sara K (integrations): SDK plan: bump major to v3, implement auto-detect fallback for streaming for 4w, add clear migration guide, and include code sample. I can own JS + Python shims.
Mike L (platform): I'll add a canary route in us-west-2 and schedule a limited rollout with deploy-bot. We'll tie it to partner feature flags so we can flip per-partner.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: partner-api-v3 -> canary group "partners-staged" at 2026-05-10T08:00Z. CI:integration-tests passed. :white_check_mark:
Raj P (vendor-eng): we'll need partner signoff matrix — who needs a direct call vs email. I'll compile partner list and mark priority.
Anna C (partnerships): good. Action items: 1) Mike — gateway + canary route (eta 2w). 2) Sara — SDK shims & migration guide (eta 3w). 3) Raj — partner impact matrix + outreach plan (eta 1w). 4) Eve — coordinate announcement copy + console banners (eta 1w). I'll set weekly syncs.
Eve M (product): for announcement copy, include explicit sample code diff, eg:
```
// v2
fetch('/chat-stream', { headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + token } })
// v3
fetch('/chat-stream', { headers: { 'Authorization': 'Redwood-Sig ' + token } })
```
Mike L (platform): testing note — include SIs in canary group (non-prod only) so they can validate streaming envelopes. Also add a perf test for the shim translation path.
Sara K (integrations): will prepare test matrix: JS/Py/.NET clients, streaming modes, reconnects, and long-running sessions. Posting as spreadsheet link once ready.
Raj P (vendor-eng): putting partners into three tiers: 1-critical (SIs + marketplace partners) 2-regular (cloud/hw partners) 3-low (experimental). I'll ask tier-1 partners for immediate calls.
Anna C (partnerships): thanks all. I'll open calendar invites for the partner calls and post the spec link once final. Ping me in this thread if any blocker. :thumbsup:
Mike L (platform): +1. I'll also create a short runbook for rollback if any partner reports broken streaming behavior.
Sara K (integrations): noted. will also add migration tests to the SDK CI so partners can run them locally.
Raj P (vendor-eng): add me to the SDK repo access list so vendor teams can fetch the shims.
Anna C (partnerships): done — added access and draft invite. Follow-ups in #partnerships weekly sync.
